source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Full Council, 14 July 2026 (Appendix A)

facts.note: Appendix A §3.5. Arithmetic ties: 62.390 - 10.839 = 51.551. Splits GF/HRA as printed. Against £20m of reserves headroom for further internal borrowing, the bulk of the £62m programme will need to come from the market unless the internal-borrowing strategy is stretched further.

facts.value: New borrowing £4.419m short-term, £0.000m long-term; debt maturing £9.295m (short £4.254m, long £5.041m); net decrease in borrowing £3.748m; total borrowing £104.923m at 31/03/26 vs £109.799m at 01/04/25

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Full Council, 14 July 2026 (Appendix A)

facts.value: Three loans rolled in year, per §4.2: PWLB Maturity £17.000m from 4.63% to 4.10%; PWLB Maturity £10.000m from 4.95% to 4.15%; LOBO £3.500m from 3.75% to 4.06% (refinanced with a PWLB maturity loan). Total refinanced: £30.500m

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Full Council, 14 July 2026 (Appendix A)

facts.note: All three refinanced rates tie exactly to our bc-loans file: loan 901490 £17m at 4.10% (matures 05/02/2028), loan 837292 £10m at 4.15% (a 6-month PWLB drawn 26/12/2025 that matured 26/6/2026), loan 910839 £3.5m at 4.06% (matures 09/03/2030). The reconciliation lead for the email is these three rates, not the aggregate — see status.note.

facts.value: Held £3.5m LOBO at 3.75% at start of year; lender exercised its option to propose 5.70% (195bp step-up); Council refused, repaid and refinanced with PWLB at 4.06%

source.title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — Full Council, 14 July 2026 (Appendix A)

Small at £3.5m but clean. Saving vs the 5.70% proposal: 164bp on £3.5m ≈ £57,400/yr; extra cost vs old 3.75% rate: 31bp ≈ £10,850/yr.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's premature repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Treasury Outturn report that went to Council on 14 July, ahead of what will be the next quarterly monitoring cycle at Audit & Accounts. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The report is clearly laid out and the balance sheet foots to the pound, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

The reason we wrote is that the three loans in your Table 4.2 all sit in our loan file at exactly the rates you print. The £17m PWLB maturity you rolled from 4.63% to 4.10% is loan 901490 on our side, maturing 5 February 2028 at 4.10%. The £10m rolled from 4.95% to 4.15% is loan 837292 — a six-month drawn on 26 December — at 4.15%. The £3.5m from the LOBO refinance is loan 910839, maturing 9 March 2030 at 4.06%. Three rates on £30.5m of in-year refinancing that we can quote back to you to the basis point. It doesn't happen every time we read a paper — three-rate matches are not the norm — and where it does, it's the shortest cross-check we can offer that the reading was real.

One honest caveat on the wider book. Your total borrowing of £104.923m at year-end is above what we hold as PWLB — 47 loans, £90.9m, weighted 3.43%. The £14m difference is almost entirely in the under-12-month bucket (your £14.1m against our £3.0m of short-dated PWLB), consistent with short-term borrowing from other councils that doesn't reach our file. Where we do hold your PWLB, the middle three buckets tie tightly to your §6.3: 8 loans totalling £23.0m in 12m-2y, 15 loans totalling £19.3m in 2-5y, 8 loans totalling £1.2m in 5-10y, each within about £20k of what you print.

The LOBO in §4.3 is the second thing worth naming. A £3.5m loan running at 3.75%, the lender proposes 5.70% — a 195 basis point step-up — you refuse, repay and refinance with PWLB at 4.06%. It is the same shape we have read repeatedly this year at Harrow, Staffordshire, Wolverhampton and Kent, and every one has been refused. We track those call windows and outcomes across the sector because no single council can see them from its own file, and this one is the latest data point.

One page you might find useful: the per-loan valuation of your book against the DMO's premature repayment curve is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis, updated daily. §4.6 says the premium charge for early repayment remained relatively expensive; that is right of the shorter, higher-coupon loans in your book, but our indicative pricing today shows the very long legacy PWLB — the £5m at 1.64% maturing 2071, the £3.5m at 1.47% maturing 2070, the £4.5m at 1.55% maturing 2045 — sitting at deep discounts. Nothing follows from it as advice: we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, and only the DMO can quote a real settlement. It is only that the shape of the discount and premium mix in your book is not what §4.6 might read as at first glance.

And for the market you would be borrowing into if you draw the £62.4m your §3.5 flags over the next two years, the monthly PWLB activity for the sector — split by HRA and General Fund, by council and by tenor — is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity. Small district books rarely see how much of the flow is going where.

On training, four fit. Reading the PWLBpredict and SONIA Forward Curve & OIS speak to your economic section 2.7 and 2.8 (Bank Rate held at 3.75%, 10-year gilts closing March at 4.92% after a spike through 5.00%). LOBO loans: the mechanics is the natural companion to §4.3. And Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets goes to the short-term borrowing you use to bridge that we can see from your maturity table but not from our file. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Sources: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 — cover paper to Full Council 14 July 2026 with Appendices 1 and A (the covering report to Audit & Accounts on 8 July and the annual treasury report body).
